task1.title: Average annual distance travelled by adults by type of travel, 1977 and 2007
task1.prompt: The table below gives information about the average annual distance travelled by adults and the types of travel in 1977 and 2007.

chartDesc.title: Average annual distance travelled by adults by type of travel in 1977 and 2007
chartDesc.yAxis: Average annual distance travelled in kilometers (km)
chartDesc.overview: Car travel was by far the most dominant mode of transportation in both years and more than doubled over the period. Overall, total distance travelled increased, driven mainly by car, taxi, and train travel, whereas distances covered by bus, walking, motorcycle, and bicycle declined.
keyFeatures: Car was the highest figure in both years, doubling from 3500 km in 1977 to 7100 km in 2007.
Taxi saw the largest proportional growth, multiplying fourfold from 200 km to 800 km.
Bus travel recorded the largest drop, decreasing from 800 km in 1977 to 500 km in 2007.
Bicycle and Motorcycle were the lowest in 1977 at 100 km each, falling to 80 km and 90 km respectively in 2007.
Train travel increased slightly from 900 km to 1000 km, making it the second highest mode in 2007.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
task1.sampleBand8:
The table compares how far the average adult travelled per year by seven modes of transport in 1977 and 2007.

Overall, total travel increased substantially over the thirty years, but the growth was driven almost entirely by cars and taxis. Distances covered by most other means — walking, cycling, motorcycling and bus travel — all contracted, suggesting a clear shift away from physically active and public forms of transport towards private, motorised ones.

The car was dominant throughout and extended its lead dramatically: the average adult drove 3,500 kilometres in 1977 but 7,100 in 2007, more than double the earlier figure and far ahead of every other mode. The most spectacular growth, however, belonged to taxis, whose figure quadrupled from 200 to 800 kilometres. Train travel also rose, though only modestly, from 900 to 1,000 kilometres.

Every other category declined. Bus travel suffered the sharpest fall, from 800 to 500 kilometres, while walking dropped by a quarter, from 400 to 300. The two-wheeled modes, never widely used, slipped further still: cycling fell from 100 to 80 kilometres a year and motorcycling from 100 to 90, leaving them the least common ways of getting around in both years.
task1.uzSampleBand8:
Jadval o'rtacha katta yoshli kishi 1977 va 2007-yillarda yetti xil transport turi bilan yiliga qancha masofa bosib o'tganini solishtiradi.

Umuman olganda, o'ttiz yil ichida umumiy qatnov sezilarli oshdi, biroq o'sish deyarli butunlay avtomobil va taksi hisobidan bo'ldi. Boshqa aksariyat vositalar — piyoda yurish, velosipeddan, mototsikldan va avtobusdan foydalanish — bo'yicha masofalar qisqardi, bu esa jismonan faol va jamoat transportidan xususiy, motorli turlarga yaqqol og'ishni ko'rsatadi.

Avtomobil boshdan-oxir yetakchi bo'lib, ustunligini keskin kengaytirdi: o'rtacha katta yoshli kishi 1977-yilda 3 500 kilometr yurgan bo'lsa, 2007-yilda 7 100 kilometr yurdi — bu avvalgi ko'rsatkichdan ikki baravardan ko'proq va boshqa barcha turlardan ancha yuqori. Biroq eng ajoyib o'sish taksiga tegishli bo'ldi: uning ko'rsatkichi 200 dan 800 kilometrga, ya'ni to'rt baravar oshdi. Poyezdda qatnov ham o'sdi, garchi kamtarona — 900 dan 1 000 kilometrgacha.

Qolgan barcha toifalar pasaydi. Avtobus qatnovi 800 dan 500 kilometrga tushib eng keskin pasayishni boshidan kechirdi, piyoda yurish esa 400 dan 300 ga — chorak qismga — kamaydi. Hech qachon keng qo'llanilmagan ikki g'ildirakli turlar yana ham pastladi: velosiped yiliga 100 dan 80 kilometrga, mototsikl 100 dan 90 ga tushdi va ular har ikkala yilda ham yurish-turishning eng kam tarqalgan usullari bo'lib qoldi.

task2.title: Getting news from the Internet instead of newspapers and TV
task2.prompt: Many people no longer read newspapers or watch TV news programmes. Instead, they get news about the world from the Internet. Is this a positive or negative development?
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
task2.sampleBand8:
Printed newspapers and television bulletins are rapidly losing their audiences as people turn to the Internet for news. In my view, this shift is on balance a positive development, although it carries genuine risks that should not be ignored.

The benefits are considerable. Online news is instantaneous and constantly updated, so readers no longer wait until the next morning to learn about events; it is also largely free and accessible to anyone with a phone, including people in places where quality papers never circulated. The Internet offers an unprecedented range of perspectives as well: instead of one national broadcaster, readers can compare foreign outlets, independent journalists and first-hand accounts, and interactive features let them question and discuss what they read rather than passively absorb it.

The disadvantages, however, are real. Online, anyone can publish, so misinformation spreads faster than corrections, and social-media algorithms tend to show users only what they already agree with, trapping them in echo chambers that deepen social division. The decline of paid journalism also starves the investigative reporting that holds governments to account. Yet these problems argue for better media literacy and sustainable funding models for serious journalism, not for a return to two broadcasts and one newspaper a day.

In conclusion, I regard the move to Internet news as broadly positive, because speed, access and diversity of information outweigh the dangers — provided readers are taught to check sources and reputable news organisations survive the transition.
task2.uzSampleBand8:
Odamlar yangilik uchun internetga yuz burgani sari bosma gazetalar va televizion axborot dasturlari auditoriyasini tez yo'qotmoqda. Mening fikrimcha, bu o'zgarish umumiy hisobda ijobiy hodisa, garchi u e'tibordan chetda qoldirib bo'lmaydigan haqiqiy xatarlarni ham o'zida saqlasa-da.

Foydalari salmoqli. Onlayn yangiliklar bir zumda yetib boradi va doimiy yangilanadi, shu bois o'quvchilar voqealardan xabar topish uchun endi ertasi kunni kutmaydi; u asosan bepul va telefoni bor har bir kishi uchun, jumladan sifatli gazetalar hech qachon yetib bormagan hududlardagi odamlar uchun ham, ochiq. Internet misli ko'rilmagan qarashlar xilma-xilligini ham taklif etadi: yagona milliy teleradiokompaniya o'rniga o'quvchilar xorijiy nashrlar, mustaqil jurnalistlar va bevosita guvohliklarni solishtira oladi, interaktiv imkoniyatlar esa o'qiganlarini passiv qabul qilish o'rniga so'roq qilish va muhokama qilishga yo'l ochadi.

Biroq kamchiliklar ham real. Internetda istalgan kishi e'lon qila oladi, shuning uchun dezinformatsiya tuzatishlardan tezroq tarqaladi, ijtimoiy tarmoq algoritmlari esa foydalanuvchilarga asosan o'zlari rozi bo'lgan narsalarni ko'rsatib, ularni ijtimoiy bo'linishni chuqurlashtiradigan aks-sado xonalariga qamab qo'yadi. Pullik jurnalistikaning inqirozi hukumatlarni javobgarlikka tortadigan surishtiruv reportajlarini ham mablag'siz qoldiradi. Ammo bu muammolar kuniga ikki teledastur va bitta gazetaga qaytishni emas, yaxshiroq mediasavodxonlik va jiddiy jurnalistika uchun barqaror moliyalashtirish modellarini talab qiladi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, internet yangiliklariga o'tishni umuman ijobiy deb bilaman, chunki tezlik, ochiqlik va axborot xilma-xilligi xatarlardan ustun keladi — faqat o'quvchilar manbalarni tekshirishga o'rgatilsa va nufuzli axborot tashkilotlari bu o'tish davridan omon chiqsa bas.
